{"id": "ae244aff-df54-448c-84b1-24345169d162", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "**Yes, the storage grows without limit, but it costs almost nothing at your current volume.**

- **Where the logs go:** Bedrock invocation logging in us-east-1 writes only to the CloudWatch log group `/llmops-demo/bedrock-invocations`. There is no S3 destination, so no bucket is accumulating data.
- **Retention:** The log group has no retention policy, so CloudWatch never expires the data. It is set to Standard class.
- **Current size:** About 124 MB is stored. The group was created about 39 days ago (mid-October), so it is growing at roughly 3 MB per day, or about 100 MB per month.
- **What that costs:** Standard CloudWatch storage is roughly $0.03 per GB-month, from my recollection of the pricing. That puts your current storage at well under a cent per month. Even a year of growth would still cost only pennies a month.

The bigger cost is ingestion, which is roughly $0.50 per GB at standard rates. That is a one-time charge when the logs are written, and a retention policy doesn't affect it. At about 100 MB per month it is also small.

The risk is mostly future growth and data hygiene. Video delivery and text delivery are both enabled, so larger prompts or higher traffic could raise the volume a lot. Invocation logs also contain full prompts and responses, so keeping them forever may not suit your data policies.

I can set a retention period on the log group, for example 30, 90 or 365 days. That change needs your approval before it runs. Tell me the period you want and I'll apply it.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
